components.description: Motivation: why variable-level causal-graph methods for fairness are impractical, motivating cluster CPDAGs.

nodes.name: Full causal graph assumption
nodes.description: Most existing causality-based fairness methods assume access to the ground-truth causal graph over an individual's features.

nodes.name: Structure learning is hard
nodes.description: Lacking perfect domain knowledge forces solving the notoriously difficult problem of learning the entire causal graph structure from observational data.

nodes.name: Restrictive functional assumptions
nodes.description: Learning the full graph relies on restrictive functional assumptions about the data-generating process, whose violations can undermine fairness guarantees.

nodes.name: CPDAG relaxation
nodes.description: Recent methods leverage a CPDAG, identifiable from conditional independence relations, to relax the full-graph assumption.

nodes.name: CPDAG estimation still hard in high dimensions
nodes.description: Estimating a CPDAG remains challenging in high-dimensional settings, requiring many conditional independence tests whose errors can accumulate and undermine fairness guarantees.

nodes.name: Cluster CPDAG needs far fewer tests
nodes.description: Cluster CPDAG inference needs substantially fewer conditional independence tests than variable-level CPDAG inference because clustering reduces graph size.

nodes.name: Research question
nodes.description: Motivates the research question: can interventional fairness be achieved using a cluster CPDAG despite unknown within-cluster causal structure?

components.description: Interventional fairness definition and its identifiability advantage.

nodes.name: Interventional fairness definition
nodes.description: Prediction is interventionally fair if the interventional distribution of the outcome is invariant to interventions on sensitive features, holding admissible features fixed (Salimi et al. 2019).

nodes.name: Group-level, interventional (not counterfactual)
nodes.description: Interventional fairness is a group-level notion defined via interventional distributions, distinct from individual-level counterfactual fairness.

nodes.name: Identifiable from partial graph knowledge
nodes.description: Interventional distributions in the fairness definition can be identified using partial causal graph knowledge, formalized as a CPDAG.

nodes.name: Back-door adjustment applicability
nodes.description: Under acyclicity and no unobserved confounders, standard back-door adjustment can be applied to identify interventional distributions.

components.description: Cluster DAGs / cluster CPDAGs and the extra structure (independence arcs, marks) they require versus plain CPDAGs.

nodes.name: Cluster DAG construction
nodes.description: A cluster graph is built by grouping nodes of a variable-level DAG according to a partition; a directed edge exists between clusters if any variable-level edge crosses between them.

nodes.name: Admissible partition assumption
nodes.description: The resulting cluster graph is assumed to be a DAG, feasible via an admissible partition designed with domain knowledge.

nodes.name: Ambiguous within-cluster conditional independence
nodes.description: Even under acyclicity, a cluster graph can entail different conditional independence relations among clusters depending on unspecified variable-level structure inside clusters (e.g., collider vs non-collider).

nodes.name: Independence arcs / marks introduced
nodes.description: Anand et al. propose independence arcs (marg/cond/never) plus connection and separation marks to explicitly represent the within-cluster ambiguity.

nodes.name: Cluster CPDAG defined
nodes.description: A cluster CPDAG expresses a cluster Markov equivalence class using directed edges, independence arcs, and connection/separation marks common to all compatible cluster DAGs, plus undirected edges that vary.

nodes.name: CLOC inference method
nodes.description: CLOC (Anand et al. 2025) infers a cluster CPDAG without restrictive assumptions about within-cluster connectivity, motivating its use as the inference backbone here.

components.description: Why cluster CPDAGs make adjustment-set identification hard, and the two-step algorithm that solves it.

nodes.name: Single adjustment set unidentifiable
nodes.description: Because a cluster CPDAG represents multiple compatible DAGs, a single adjustment set Z cannot be identified for back-door adjustment.

nodes.name: Enumerate multiple candidate sets
nodes.description: The proposed solution is to enumerate adjustment sets Z1,...,ZM such that at least one is valid for the true cluster DAG.

nodes.name: Variable-level enumeration methods don't transfer
nodes.description: Efficient enumeration methods for variable-level CPDAGs rely on graphical properties (e.g., chordality) that cluster CPDAGs lack.

nodes.name: Novel enumeration algorithm needed
nodes.description: A novel adjustment-set enumeration algorithm is developed that explicitly accounts for independence arcs and separation/connection marks.

nodes.name: Step 1: Parent set enumeration
nodes.description: First enumerate candidate parent sets of sensitive features A (definite parents plus possible-parent subsets of siblings satisfying Theorem 3.5).

nodes.name: Step 2: Adjustment set completion
nodes.description: If parent sets contain connection-marked clusters, iteratively augment each candidate set via Algorithm 1's queue-based propagation to achieve d-separation.

nodes.name: Refinement fallback for FAIL cases
nodes.description: When Algorithm 1 cannot guarantee identifiability (FAIL), the cluster CPDAG is refined by splitting connection-marked clusters into singleton nodes and re-inferring, at worst reaching variable-level granularity.

components.description: Worst-case unfairness penalty and the computational bottleneck it creates.

nodes.name: True valid Zm unknown
nodes.description: It is uncertain which of Z1,...,ZM yields a valid adjustment for the true cluster DAG.

nodes.name: Worst-case penalty formulation
nodes.description: The unfairness penalty is defined as the maximum, over m, of the aggregated kernel MMD between interventional distribution pairs.

nodes.name: Naive computation is prohibitive
nodes.description: Naively computing this worst-case MMD requires O(M·NA^2·NXad·n^2) time, which is computationally prohibitive.

nodes.name: Need for efficient MMD estimation
nodes.description: This prohibitive cost motivates developing efficient estimation strategies for the penalty function.

components.description: The barycenter-MMD + random-Fourier-feature strategy that resolves the computational bottleneck.

nodes.name: Barycenter MMD decomposition
nodes.description: Pairwise MMD summation over sensitive-value pairs (a,a') is rewritten as a sum of MMDs to a barycenter (mixture) distribution, reducing O(NA^2) to O(NA).

nodes.name: RFF approximation of kernel
nodes.description: The feature map of the MMD kernel is approximated with dRFF-dimensional random Fourier features, reducing per-MMD cost from O(n^2) to O(n·dRFF).

nodes.name: IPW-weighted kernel mean embedding estimator
nodes.description: Combining inverse probability weighting with RFFs yields a weighted empirical estimator of the kernel mean embedding for each interventional distribution.

nodes.name: Overall complexity reduced
nodes.description: Combining barycenter decomposition and RFF approximation reduces overall worst-case MMD computation to O(M·NA·NXad·n·dRFF).

nodes.name: Mellowmax relaxation of max
nodes.description: Since the max over m in the penalty is non-differentiable, it is approximated with the Mellowmax function to enable gradient-based training.

components.description: Synthetic experiment results: C-IFair vs baselines across cluster counts and settings.

nodes.name: C-IFair best among practical baselines (synthetic)
nodes.description: Excluding Oracle and Full, C-IFair achieves the best RMSE and unfairness across all synthetic settings (d=5,10,15; linear and nonlinear).

nodes.name: C-IFair closest to Oracle
nodes.description: C-IFair achieves fairness closest to Oracle while maintaining high accuracy, despite Oracle requiring the unrealistic true variable-level DAG.

nodes.name: Unaware/No-DesCs insufficient
nodes.description: Unaware and No-DesCs exhibit high RMSE and unfairness, implying that simply discarding predictive features fails to remove indirect discriminatory effects.

nodes.name: ε-IFair/ℓ-IFair degrade at high dimension
nodes.description: ε-IFair and ℓ-IFair produce less fair predictions than C-IFair in high-dimensional setups (d=15), indicating inferred variable-level CPDAGs become unreliable there.

nodes.name: Cluster CPDAGs more reliable at scale
nodes.description: Cluster CPDAG inference is more reliable than variable-level CPDAG inference in high-dimensional setups, explaining C-IFair's relative advantage at d=15.

nodes.name: λ trade-off confirmed
nodes.description: Varying penalty weight λ from 0 to 200 shows increasing λ reduces unfairness at the cost of higher RMSE, confirming C-IFair can flexibly tune the fairness-accuracy trade-off.

components.description: Real-world dataset results and fairness illustration.

nodes.name: C-IFair best on real-world AUC/unfairness
nodes.description: Excluding Oracle and Full, C-IFair achieves the best AUC and unfairness among all baselines on Adult, German credit, and OULAD datasets.

nodes.name: Practical utility underscored
nodes.description: The real-world results underscore C-IFair's practical utility for real-world fairness applications.

nodes.name: Fairness illustration on Adult
nodes.description: Comparing inferred interventional distributions of Ŷ across sensitive-feature interventions on Adult shows C-IFair makes sufficiently fair predictions with respect to gender and race.

components.description: Contribution summary chain: cluster-graph algorithm -> learning framework -> empirical validation.

nodes.name: Contribution 1: adjustment cluster set algorithm
nodes.description: A graphical algorithm to enumerate adjustment cluster sets, at least one of which enables identification of interventional distributions for the true cluster DAG.

nodes.name: Contribution 2: worst-case fairness learning framework
nodes.description: A learning framework that achieves interventional fairness by penalizing worst-case unfairness across adjustment cluster sets, using an efficient barycenter kernel MMD.

nodes.name: Contribution 3: empirical validation
nodes.description: Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate a better fairness-accuracy trade-off than existing approaches.

isolated_nodes.name: Legal alignment of causal fairness
isolated_nodes.description: Causal notions of fairness align with legal requirements since discrimination is often legally assessed via the causal relationship between decisions and sensitive attributes.

isolated_nodes.name: Future work: cluster MPDAGs
isolated_nodes.description: Extending cluster CPDAGs to cluster MPDAGs is highly non-trivial but would further reduce structural uncertainty and improve the fairness-accuracy trade-off; left to future work.
